recent_events.title: Timur Ibragimov appointed Chairman of the Management Board
recent_events.description: Effective January 2026, Timur Ibragimov became Chairman of the Management Board (CEO), transitioning from his prior role as Chairman of the Board of Directors. Sergey Ibragimov joined the Board of Directors. The bank adopted a corporate governance model separating ownership and operational management, in line with international financial-institution standards.
recent_events.impact: Modernizes governance; signals transparency to international partners and investors.

recent_events.title: Extraordinary shareholders' meeting approves governance reform
recent_events.description: On 22 December 2025, an extraordinary general meeting of shareholders formalized the leadership transition and adopted a management model typical of large international financial organizations, separating ownership from executive management.
recent_events.impact: Strengthens corporate governance framework and institutional credibility.

recent_events.title: CEO Umut Abakirova meets U.S. Treasury Secretary and Wall Street executives
recent_events.description: CEO Umut Abakirova held talks with U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and executives from BlackRock, Bank of America and KPMG in Washington DC, positioning Bakai Bank as a gateway for U.S. investment into Central Asia and discussing cooperation in banking, private investment and critical minerals (rare earths, lithium).
recent_events.impact: Elevated the bank's international profile; advanced U.S.-Kyrgyz economic engagement.

recent_events.title: Bakai Bank ranked among global leaders in S&P Global CSA 2025
recent_events.description: Bakai Bank received its first Corporate Sustainability Assessment (CSA) score from S&P Global, entering the 85th percentile of global banks and becoming one of Central Asia's leading banks in sustainable development, assessed alongside over 12,000 companies worldwide.
recent_events.impact: Strengthened ESG credentials; improved access to international capital.

recent_events.title: Strategic partnership with UFC as official bank in CIS
recent_events.description: Bakai Bank became the official banking partner of UFC (Ultimate Fighting Championship) in nine CIS countries including Armenia, Azerbaijan and across Central Asia, substantially boosting the bank's brand visibility beyond the finance sector.
recent_events.impact: Major brand and marketing milestone; expanded regional footprint.

recent_events.title: Shareholders approve capital increase to KGS 10 billion
recent_events.description: At the extraordinary general meeting of shareholders on 14 May 2025, OJSC Bakai Bank approved an increase of charter capital by nearly KGS 3 billion (to approximately KGS 10 billion) and the distribution of 2024 profits. Quorum was 84.95%.
recent_events.impact: Reinforced capital base to support lending growth and regulatory buffers.

recent_events.title: Bakai Bank joins UN Global Compact
recent_events.description: From March 2025, Bakai Bank became a participant of the United Nations Global Compact, the world's largest corporate sustainability initiative, reaffirming its commitment to ESG principles.
recent_events.impact: Anchored ESG strategy within a globally recognized framework.

core_business: Universal commercial bank providing a full range of banking services to retail customers, SMEs and corporate clients. Core offerings include payment cards, consumer and business loans, deposits, money transfers, online/mobile banking, trade finance and treasury operations. The bank operates an extensive branch network across Kyrgyzstan (7 branches plus savings cashier outlets in Bishkek, Osh, Tokmok, Karakol, Jalal-Abad, Kara-Balta and Bosteri/Issyk-Kul) and maintains correspondent relationships with leading banks worldwide and across CIS countries. Licensed by the National Bank of the Kyrgyz Republic (license No. 043, issued 28 December 1998).
apec_stance: Bakai Bank is positioning itself as a regional financial gateway for Central Asia, actively courting U.S. and international investors. Under CEO Umut Abakirova's leadership (2025), the bank met with U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Wall Street firms (BlackRock, Bank of America, KPMG) to promote Kyrgyzstan as a hub for American capital in emerging markets, including critical minerals (rare earths, lithium). The bank maintains correspondent relationships with leading global banks and CIS-country institutions, joined the UN Global Compact in March 2025, became an S&P Global CSA top-percentile bank in August 2025, and serves multinational clients such as Coca-Cola, KFC and General Electric. While Kyrgyzstan is not an APEC member, the bank's internationalization strategy, ESG integration and role as a UFC CIS partner demonstrate active engagement with Asia-Pacific and global markets, aligning with regional connectivity and sustainable-finance agendas.
profile: OJSC Bakai Bank (ОАО «Бакай Банк», license NBKR No. 043 of 28 December 1998) is one of the largest universal commercial banks in Kyrgyzstan, operating as an open joint-stock company. Founded in 1998 and headquartered in Bishkek, the bank has built a 25+ year track record and was named Kyrgyzstan's best bank by financial results three years running (2002-2004), with podium finishes in 2005 and 2006. As of 2024 it ranks among the country's top three banks by retail deposits. The bank serves over one million clients, having doubled its loan portfolio within two years, and counts international brands such as Coca-Cola, KFC and General Electric among its corporate clients. In 2025 Bakai Bank became an official partner of UFC in the CIS region, joined the UN Global Compact, received a strong debut score in the S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment (85th percentile of global banks), and increased its charter capital to approximately KGS 10 billion. In January 2026 the bank adopted an international-standard governance model with Timur Ibragimov as Chairman of the Management Board and his father Sergey Ibragimov (largest shareholder, ~71% stake historically) on the Board of Directors.
